kept.title: Corpus-backed storage drops debouncing and write serialization
kept.desc: Unlike `createDebouncedLocalStorage`, the CorpusFS-backed `setItem` writes the whole persist blob on *every* `set()` (i.e. every keystroke) with no debounce and no queue, so overlapping async `writeFile` calls to the same OPFS file race; OPFS `createWritable()` takes an exclusive lock, so concurrent writes will reject with `NoModificationAllowedError` (mapped to `{kind:"io"}`) and/or land out of order, silently losing state.

kept.title: "Dev-only" flag has no dev guard
kept.desc: The doc comment and CLAUDE.md both state the flag is "DEV-ONLY", but `isCorpusEnabled()` honors `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1` in production builds and the `corpus-fs-enabled` localStorage key in any browser; given enabling it means starting from an empty corpus with no migration, the missing `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` check makes the claim misleading and the footgun real.

kept.title: Fail-loud manifest codec silently drops malformed array entries
kept.desc: `raw.sources.filter(isObject)`, `raw.artifacts.filter(isObject)` and `customTypeIds.filter(typeof x === "string")` discard non-conforming entries instead of failing, so a partially corrupted `workspace.json` parses "successfully" with fewer sources/artifacts — exactly the "masquerades as no work / masks data loss" outcome the header says parsing must prevent. `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are likewise silently defaulted to `now`.

kept.title: `finally { await w.close() }` can mask the quota error it is supposed to reify
kept.desc: Real OPFS surfaces quota failures on `write()`/`close()`; if `write()` rejects, the unconditional `await w.close()` in `finally` will typically reject too (errored/closed stream) and that second error replaces the original, so the failure is mapped to `{kind:"io"}` instead of `{kind:"quota-exceeded"}`. The G7 test only stubs `createWritable()` throwing, so this realistic path is untested — consider `abort()`/try-catching the close and preserving the first error.
